text.p: headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Alan Eagleson faces eight charges: Allegations of fraud, theft against former hockey czar involve Canada Cup tournaments.
- Bomb explodes in Paris subway: Jacques Chirac condemns 'act of barbarity.'
- Ontario government tightlipped on Indian clash: Protester's family baffled by stand.
- Costly consultants to trim public jobs: Advisers to earn up to $2,625 a day.
- Afghan catastrophe looms, UN warns: World body pushes for doubling of aid.
- Kidnapped teen escapes pimps' clutches: Abducted before she was to testify, girl was held six weeks, forced to work street, police say.
- Bre-X suitors race to deadline: List of potential partners grows, as does estimate of contested Busang gold depostit.
- Placer Dome chief no stranger to a fight: Investors give John Wilson praise for valour, although few expect him to succeed in his effort to gain a chunk of the massive Bre-X gold find.
- House sales soaring: Toronto, Vancouver gains spark building boom forecast.
- Canadian Airlines gets low-key reception from creditors: Carrier armed with AMR Corp concession.
- Countdown for Bre-X: On the brink of Indonesia's deadline for a development deal with Barrick, Bre-X issues an even more glowing report on the potential of its gold find.
- The battle for hearts, minds and control at ISG.
